title.zh: 卷六十二 列傳第二十二 羊欣 張敷 王微
title.en: Volume 62 Biographies 22: Yang Xin, Zhang Fu, Wang Wei
title.raw: 卷六十二 列傳第二十二 羊欣 張敷 王微 Volume 62 Biographies 22: Yang Xin, Zhang Fu, Wang Wei

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十二 羊欣張敷王微

translations.literal: Biographies 22: Yang Xin, Zhang Fu, and Wang Wei
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 22: Yang Xin, Zhang Fu, and Wang Wei

sentences.zh: 羊欣，字敬元，泰山南城人也。

translations.literal: Yang Xin, styled Jingyuan, was a man of Nancheng in Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xin, whose courtesy name was Jingyuan, came from Nancheng in Taishan commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖忱，晉徐州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Chen was Jin Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chen had served as inspector of Xuzhou under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖權，黃門郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Quan was a Yellow Gate Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Quan had been a gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 父不疑，桂陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Buyi was Administrator of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Buyi had served as administrator of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 欣少靖默，無競於人，美言笑，善容止。

translations.literal: Xin in youth was quiet and reserved, not contending with others, fine in speech and laughter, and skilled in bearing and deportment.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Xin was quiet and unassuming, never striving against others; he spoke gracefully, laughed pleasantly, and carried himself with natural elegance.

sentences.zh: 汎覽經籍，尤長隸書。

translations.literal: He broadly perused the classics, and was especially accomplished in clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and was especially accomplished in clerical script calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 不疑初為烏程令，欣時年十二，時王獻之為吳興太守，甚知愛之。

translations.literal: When Buyi was first magistrate of Wucheng, Xin was twelve years old; at that time Wang Xianzhi was Administrator of Wuxing and came to know and love him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Buyi was first appointed magistrate of Wucheng, Xin was twelve; Wang Xianzhi was then administrator of Wuxing and took a great liking to him.

sentences.zh: 獻之嘗夏月入縣，欣著新絹裙晝寢，獻之書裙數幅而去。

translations.literal: Xianzhi once entered the county in midsummer; Xin was wearing a new silk skirt and napping by day; Xianzhi wrote several panels on the skirt and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Once in midsummer Xianzhi came into the county seat and found Xin napping in a new silk skirt; he wrote several lines on the skirt and left.

sentences.zh: 欣本工書，因此彌善。

translations.literal: Xin was originally skilled at writing; because of this he became still better.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was already skilled at calligraphy, and this episode made him still better.

sentences.zh: 起家輔國參軍，府解還家。

translations.literal: He began his career as Aide to the Army Supporting the State; when the office was dissolved he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as aide to the army of the Supporting-the-State commandery and returned home when that post was abolished.

sentences.zh: 隆安中，朝廷漸亂，欣優遊私門，不復進仕。

translations.literal: In the Long'an era the court gradually fell into disorder; Xin took his ease within his private household and no longer advanced in office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Long'an years, as the court grew increasingly chaotic, Xin kept to his private life and sought no further advancement.

sentences.zh: 會稽王世子元顯每使欣書，常辭不奉命，元顯怒，乃以為其後軍府舍人。

translations.literal: Sima Yuanxian, heir apparent of the Princedom of Kuaiji, repeatedly had Xin write for him; Xin often declined and would not obey the order; Yuanxian was angry and therefore made him a clerk in his Rear Army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yuanxian, heir apparent of Kuaiji, often asked Xin to write for him; Xin habitually refused, and Yuanxian in anger appointed him clerk in his rear-army headquarters.

sentences.zh: 此職本用寒人，欣意貌恬然，不以高卑見色，論者稱焉。

translations.literal: This post was originally filled by men of humble birth; Xin's expression and bearing were tranquil, and he did not show his feelings according to rank high or low; commentators praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: The post was normally given to men of humble birth, yet Xin remained serene in look and manner and showed no change of color whether treated high or low; observers praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 欣嘗詣領軍將軍謝混，混拂席改服，然後見之。

translations.literal: Xin once called on the General Commanding the Army Xie Hun; Hun brushed the mat and changed his garments, and only then received him.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Xin called on the commanding general Xie Hun, Hun brushed the mat and changed his clothes before receiving him.

sentences.zh: 時混族子靈運在坐，退告族兄瞻曰：「望蔡見羊欣，遂易衣改席。

translations.literal: At the time Hun's clansman Lingyun was seated there; he withdrew and told his clansman elder brother Zhan, saying: "When Wangcai received Yang Xin, he at once changed clothes and brushed the mat."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun, a kinsman of Hun's, was present; afterward he told his elder cousin Zhan, "When Wangcai received Yang Xin, he changed his clothes and brushed the mat."

sentences.zh: 」欣由此益知名。

translations.literal: From this Xin became still more renowned.
translations.idiomatic: From this episode Xin became still more widely known.

sentences.zh: 桓玄輔政，領平西將軍，以欣為平西參軍，仍轉主簿，參預機要。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan assisted in government and held the post of General Pacifying the West, he made Xin an aide on his staff; he was then transferred to chief clerk and took part in confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan held power as regent and also served as General Pacifying the West, he appointed Xin an aide on his staff, then chief clerk, entrusting him with confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 欣欲自疏，時漏密事，玄覺其此意，愈重之，以為楚臺殿中郎。

translations.literal: Xin wished to distance himself; he would at times leak secret matters; Xuan perceived this intention and valued him all the more, appointing him Palace Attendant of the Chu Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to keep his distance, Xin sometimes leaked confidential matters; Xuan perceived his intent and valued him all the more, appointing him palace attendant of the Chu Terrace.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「尚書政事之本，殿中禮樂所出。

translations.literal: He said to him: "The Secretariat is the root of governmental affairs; the Palace is where ritual and music proceed from."
translations.idiomatic: He told him, "The Secretariat is the root of government; the palace service is where ritual and music take their form."

sentences.zh: 卿昔處股肱，方此為輕也。

translations.literal: You formerly stood in the position of the ruler's right arm; compared with that, this is light.
translations.idiomatic: You once stood at the ruler's right hand; this post is lighter by comparison."

sentences.zh: 」欣拜職少日，稱病自免，屏居里巷，十餘年不出。

translations.literal: " Xin had accepted the post only a few days when he pleaded illness and resigned, secluding himself in lanes and alleys and not going out for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Xin had held the post only a few days when he pleaded illness and resigned, living secluded in his neighborhood for more than ten years without going abroad.

sentences.zh: 義熙中，弟徽被遇於高祖，高祖謂諮議參軍鄭鮮之曰：「羊徽一時美器，世論猶在兄後，恨不識之。

translations.literal: In the Yixi era his younger brother Hui won favor with the Founding Emperor; the Founding Emperor said to Adviser Zheng Xianzhi: "Yang Hui is a fine vessel of the age; public opinion still places him after his elder brother—I regret not having known him."
translations.idiomatic: During the Yixi years his younger brother Hui came into favor with Emperor Wu; the emperor said to adviser Zheng Xianzhi, "Yang Hui is a rare talent of the day, yet opinion still ranks him below his elder brother—I regret never having met the elder."

sentences.zh: 」即板欣補右將軍劉藩司馬，轉長史，中軍將軍道憐諮議參軍。

translations.literal: " He thereupon appointed Xin by provisional commission as marshal to the Right General Liu Fan, then transferred him to chief clerk and made him adviser to the Central Army General Dao Lin.
translations.idiomatic: He at once appointed Xin marshal on the staff of the Right General Liu Fan, then chief clerk, and adviser to the Central Army general Dao Lin.

sentences.zh: 出為新安太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 在郡四年，簡惠著稱。

translations.literal: During four years in the commandery he was noted for simplicity and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: During four years in the commandery he won renown for simple, benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 除臨川王義慶輔國長史，廬陵王義真車騎諮議參軍，並不就。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk Assisting the State to the Prince of Linchuan Liu Yiqing and Adviser to the Chariots and Cavalry of the Prince of Luling Liu Yizhen, but did not take either post.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk assisting the state on the staff of Prince Linchuan Liu Yiqing and adviser to the chariots-and-cavalry staff of Prince Luling Liu Yizhen, but accepted neither post.

sentences.zh: 太祖重之，以為新安太守，前後凡十三年，遊玩山水，甚得適性。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor valued him and made him Administrator of Xin'an; for thirteen years in all he roamed mountains and waters and found the life very much to his nature.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen valued him and kept him as administrator of Xin'an; for thirteen years in all he wandered among mountains and streams and found the life deeply congenial.

sentences.zh: 轉在義興，非其好也。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Yixing, which was not to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to Yixing, it did not suit his taste.

sentences.zh: 頃之，又稱病篤自免歸。

translations.literal: Before long he again pleaded grave illness and resigned to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he again pleaded serious illness and resigned to go home.

sentences.zh: 除中散大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grandee Remonstrant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grandee remonstrant.

sentences.zh: 素好黃老，常手自書章，有病不服藥，飲符水而已。

translations.literal: He had long favored Huang-Lao teachings, often copied talismanic texts with his own hand, and when ill would not take medicine but drank only talisman water.
translations.idiomatic: He had long favored Huang-Lao teachings, often copied talisman texts himself, and when ill refused medicine, drinking only talisman water.

sentences.zh: 兼善醫術，撰《藥方》十卷。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in medicine and compiled ten juan of Prescriptions.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled in medicine and compiled a ten-juan work entitled Prescriptions.

sentences.zh: 欣以不堪拜伏，辭不朝覲，高祖、太祖並恨不識之。

translations.literal: Because Xin could not bear to bow and prostrate himself, he declined court audiences; both the Founding Emperor and the Founding Emperor's successor regretted not having known him.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bear bowing and prostration, Xin declined court audiences; both Emperor Wu and Emperor Wen regretted never having met him in person.

sentences.zh: 自非尋省近親，不妄行詣，行必由城外，未嘗入六關。

translations.literal: Unless visiting close kin on condolence calls, he would not go out on visits at random; when he traveled he always went by routes outside the walls and never entered the Six Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Except when paying condolence visits to close kin, he never called on anyone casually; when he went out he always kept to roads outside the city walls and never passed through the six inner gates.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十九年，卒，時年七十三。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Yuanjia he died, at the age of seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Yuanjia he died, aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 子俊，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Jun died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun died young.

sentences.zh: 弟徽，字敬猷，世譽多欣。

translations.literal: His younger brother Hui, styled Jingyou, won more praise in the world than Xin.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Hui, courtesy name Jingyou, enjoyed greater contemporary renown than Xin.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮京口，以為記室參軍掌事。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor held Jingkou, he made Hui Recording Secretary Aide in charge of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu held Jingkou, he appointed Hui recording secretary on his staff, in charge of affairs.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷中書郎，直西省。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to Gentleman of the Secretariat and served in the Western Department.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to gentleman of the secretariat and served in the western office.

sentences.zh: 後為太祖西中郎長史、河東太守。

translations.literal: Later he became Chief Clerk to the Western Central Army General for Emperor Wen and Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served Emperor Wen as chief clerk on the western central-army staff and as administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 子瞻，元嘉末為世祖南中郎長史、尋陽太守，卒官。

translations.literal: His son Zhan, at the end of Yuanjia, was Chief Clerk to the Southern Central Army General for Emperor Xiaowu and Administrator of Xunyang, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhan, at the end of Yuanjia, served Emperor Xiaowu as chief clerk on the southern central-army staff and as administrator of Xunyang, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 張敷，字景胤，吳郡人，吳興太守邵子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Fu, styled Jingyin, was a man of Wu commandery and the son of the Administrator of Wuxing, Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu, courtesy name Jingyin, was a native of Wu commandery and the son of Shao, administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 生而母沒。

translations.literal: His mother died when he was born.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died when he was born.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，問母所在，家人告以死生之分，敷雖童蒙，便有思慕之色。

translations.literal: When he was several years old he asked where his mother was; the household told him of the separation between life and death; though Fu was still a child, he already showed the look of longing.
translations.idiomatic: When he was only a few years old he asked where his mother was; the family explained that she was gone forever; though still a small child, he already wore the look of one who mourned her.

sentences.zh: 年十許歲，求母遺物，而散施已盡，唯得一畫扇，乃緘錄之，每至感思，輒開笥流涕。

translations.literal: When he was about ten he sought his mother's surviving objects, but what had been distributed was already gone; he obtained only one painted fan, which he sealed and kept; whenever longing moved him he would open the chest and weep.
translations.idiomatic: At about ten he asked for his mother's belongings, but everything had already been given away; he found only a painted fan, which he sealed away; whenever grief overcame him he would open the chest and weep.

sentences.zh: 見從母，常悲感哽咽。

translations.literal: When he saw his father's concubine who had been like a mother to him, he would often choke with grief.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw his aunt by marriage he would choke with grief.

sentences.zh: 性整貴，風韻甚高，好讀玄書，兼屬文論，少有盛名。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and noble, his bearing very elevated; he loved to read arcane texts and was also skilled in literary discourse; from youth he enjoyed great fame.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and fastidious by nature, with a lofty bearing, he loved arcane learning and was also skilled at literary composition; he won early renown.

sentences.zh: 高祖見而愛之，以為世子中軍參軍，數見接引。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor saw him and loved him, making him an aide in the heir apparent's central army, and repeatedly received and guided him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu took a liking to him and appointed him aide in the crown prince's central-army staff, summoning him often for guidance.

sentences.zh: 永初初，遷秘書郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongchu he was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongchu he was promoted to gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嘗在省直，中書令傅亮貴宿權要，聞其好學，過候之；

translations.literal: Once while on duty in the office, the Secretariat Director Fu Liang, a senior man of weight and power, heard that he loved learning and came to call on him;
translations.idiomatic: Once while on duty at court, Fu Liang, the secretariat director—a senior figure of great influence—heard of his love of learning and came to call on him;

sentences.zh: 敷臥不即起，亮怪而去。

translations.literal: Fu was lying down and did not rise at once; Liang took it as strange and left.
translations.idiomatic: Fu remained lying down and did not rise at once; Liang took offense and left.

sentences.zh: 父邵為湘州，去官侍從。

translations.literal: When his father Shao was in Xiangzhou, he left office to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Shao went to Xiangzhou, he left his post to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 太祖版為西中郎參軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen appointed him by provisional commission as an aide to the Western Central Army General.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen appointed him by provisional commission as aide on the western central-army staff.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，為員外散騎侍郎，秘書丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia he was Extraordinary Gentleman of the Palace Cavalry and Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanjia he served as extraordinary gentleman of the palace cavalry and secretary of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭鎮江陵，以為撫軍功曹，轉記室參軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jiangxia Liu Yigong held Jiangling, he made Fu Merit Officer on the Pacifying Army staff, then transferred him to Recording Secretary Aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jiangxia Liu Yigong held Jiangling, he appointed Fu merit officer on his pacifying-army staff, then recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 時義恭就太祖求一學義沙門，比沙門求見發遣，會敷赴假還江陵，太祖謂沙門曰：「張敷應西，當令相載。

translations.literal: At that time Yigong asked the emperor for a monk learned in doctrine; just as the monk sought an audience to be sent off, Fu happened to be returning on leave to Jiangling; the emperor said to the monk: "Zhang Fu is going west—you should have him carry you along."
translations.idiomatic: Yigong had asked the emperor for a monk learned in doctrine; just as the monk was seeking leave to depart, Fu happened to be returning on leave to Jiangling; the emperor told the monk, "Zhang Fu is going west—you should travel with him."

sentences.zh: 」及敷辭，上謂曰：「撫軍須一意懷道人，卿可以後艑載之，道中可得言晤。

translations.literal: " When Fu took leave, the emperor said to him: "The Pacifying Army needs a single-minded man of the Way; you may carry him in the rear boat, and on the road you can converse together."
translations.idiomatic: When Fu came to take his leave, the emperor said, "The pacifying-army command needs a devoted man of the Way; you may take him in the rear boat and talk with him on the journey."

sentences.zh: 」敷不奉旨，曰：「臣性不耐雜。

translations.literal: " Fu did not obey the order and said: "Your servant by nature cannot endure a crowd."
translations.idiomatic: Fu declined the order, saying, "Your servant by nature cannot bear mixed company."

sentences.zh: 」上甚不說。

translations.literal: " The emperor was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 遷正員郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regular gentleman.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人狄當、周赳並管要務，以敷同省名家，欲詣之。

translations.literal: The Secretariat Clerks Di Dang and Zhou Jiu both managed important affairs; because Fu was a famous man of the same office, they wished to call on him.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat clerks Di Dang and Zhou Jiu both handled weighty affairs; seeing Fu as a famous man of the same office, they wished to call on him.

sentences.zh: 赳曰：「彼若不相容，便不如不往。

translations.literal: Jiu said: "If he will not tolerate us, we had better not go."
translations.idiomatic: Jiu said, "If he will not tolerate us, we had better not go."

sentences.zh: 詎可輕往邪？

translations.literal: How can one go lightly?
translations.idiomatic: How can we go so lightly?"

sentences.zh: 」當曰：「吾等並已員外郎矣，何憂不得共坐。

translations.literal: " Dang said: "We are already extraordinary gentlemen—why worry that we cannot sit together?"
translations.idiomatic: Dang said, "We are already extraordinary gentlemen—why worry that we cannot sit together?"

sentences.zh: 」敷先設二床，去壁三四尺，二客就席，酬接甚歡，既而呼左右曰：「移我遠客。

translations.literal: " Fu first set out two couches three or four feet from the wall; the two guests took their seats and the exchange was very pleasant; then he called to his attendants, saying: "Move me away from these distant guests."
translations.idiomatic: Fu first set out two couches three or four feet from the wall; the two guests sat down and the conversation went pleasantly enough; then he called to his attendants, "Move me away from these distant guests."

sentences.zh: 」赳等失色而去。

translations.literal: " Jiu and the others turned pale and left.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu and the others turned pale and left.

sentences.zh: 其自摽遇如此。

translations.literal: In his self-estimation and treatment of others it was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the way he held himself and treated others.

sentences.zh: 善持音儀，盡詳緩之致，與人別，執手曰：「念相聞。

translations.literal: He was skilled in maintaining tone and bearing, exhausting the effect of measured ease; when parting from others he would take their hands and say: "Think of keeping in touch."
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in tone and bearing, carrying unhurried grace to its fullest; when he parted from someone he would take his hand and say, "Remember to let me hear from you."

sentences.zh: 」餘響久之不絕。

translations.literal: " The lingering sound long did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: The lingering cadence of his voice would long not fade.

sentences.zh: 張氏後進至今慕之，其源流起自敷也。

translations.literal: Later members of the Zhang clan admire him to this day; the current of their style begins with Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations of the Zhang clan still admire him; the style they follow begins with Fu.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門侍郎，始興王濬後軍長史，司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate, Chief Clerk of the Rear Army of the Prince of Shixing Liu Jun, and Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gate, chief clerk on Prince Shixing Liu Jun's rear-army staff, and left chief clerk of the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 未拜，父在吳興亡，報以疾篤，敷往奔省，自發都至吳興成服，凡十餘日，始進水漿。

translations.literal: Before he had accepted the appointment, his father died in Wuxing; when word came that he was gravely ill, Fu hurried to attend him; from leaving the capital until putting on mourning garments in Wuxing, more than ten days in all passed before he first took water or broth.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the appointment, word came that his father was dying in Wuxing; Fu rushed home; from leaving the capital until donning mourning garb in Wuxing more than ten days passed before he took even water or broth.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，不進鹽菜，遂毀瘠成疾。

translations.literal: When the burial was finished he took no salted food or vegetables, and thus wasted away into illness.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he ate no salted food or vegetables and wasted away into serious illness.

sentences.zh: 世父茂度每止譬之，輒更感慟，絕而復續。

translations.literal: His uncle by the senior line Maodu would each time stop and admonish him, but he would only grieve the more, fainting and reviving again.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Maodu would try each time to comfort him, but Fu only grieved the more, fainting and coming to again.

sentences.zh: 茂度曰：「我冀譬汝有益，但更甚耳。

translations.literal: Maodu said: "I hoped comforting you would help, but it only makes it worse."
translations.idiomatic: Maodu said, "I hoped comforting you would help, but it only makes things worse."

sentences.zh: 」自是不復往。

translations.literal: " From then on he did not go again.
translations.idiomatic: After that he stopped visiting.

sentences.zh: 未朞而卒，時年四十一。

translations.literal: Before the mourning period was out he died, at the age of forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Before the mourning year was out he died, aged forty-one.

sentences.zh: 琅邪顏延之書弔茂度曰：「賢弟子少履貞規，長懷理要，清風素氣，得之天然。

translations.literal: Yan Yanzhi of Langye wrote to condole with Maodu, saying: "Your worthy nephew in youth practiced pure conduct, in maturity cherished the essentials of principle, clear wind and plain spirit—he possessed these by nature."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yanzhi of Langye wrote to condole with Maodu: "Your worthy nephew in youth upheld pure conduct; in maturity he cherished the essentials of principle; clear bearing and plain spirit were his by nature."

sentences.zh: 言面以來，便申忘年之好，比雖艱隔成阻，而情問無睽。

translations.literal: Since we spoke face to face we formed a friendship that ignored age; though lately hardship and separation have become obstacles, our feelings and inquiries have not grown estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Since we met in person we formed a friendship that ignored the difference in age; though distance and hardship have lately come between us, affection and regard have not grown cold."

sentences.zh: 薄莫之人，冀其方見慰說，豈謂中年，奄為長往，聞問悼心，有兼恆痛。

translations.literal: A man in the twilight of life, I hoped soon to see him again for comfort and talk—who would have thought that in midlife he would suddenly go on the long journey? News of it grieves the heart with a grief beyond ordinary sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: I am myself near evening; I had hoped soon to see him again for comfort and talk—who would have thought that in midlife he would suddenly depart forever? The news fills my heart with a grief beyond ordinary sorrow.

sentences.zh: 足下門教敦至，兼實家寶，一旦喪失，何可為懷。

translations.literal: Your household instruction is sincere and thorough, and he was moreover a true treasure of the family; to lose him in a single day—how can one contain one's grief?
translations.idiomatic: Your household discipline is sincere and thorough, and he was moreover a true treasure of the clan; to lose him in a single day—how can grief be contained?"

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: " In such fashion was he esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，詔曰：「司徒故左長史張敷，貞心簡立，幼樹風規。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, an edict said: "The former Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works Zhang Fu had a loyal heart and simple integrity, and from youth established moral standards."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, an edict said, "The late left chief clerk of the minister of works, Zhang Fu, possessed a loyal heart and simple integrity and from youth established moral standards."

sentences.zh: 居哀毀滅，孝道淳至，宜在追甄，於以報美。

translations.literal: In mourning he destroyed himself in grief; his filial devotion was pure and utmost; he should be posthumously honored, thereby repaying his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he destroyed himself through grief; his filial devotion was pure and complete; he should be posthumously honored to repay his excellence."

sentences.zh: 可追贈侍中。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Attendant Within.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously granted attendant within.

sentences.zh: 」於是改其所居稱為孝張里。

translations.literal: " Thereupon his former residence was renamed Filial Zhang Lane.
translations.idiomatic: His former residence was then renamed Filial Zhang Lane.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons.

sentences.zh: 王微，字景玄，琅邪臨沂人，太保弘弟子也。

translations.literal: Wang Wei, styled Jingxuan, was a man of Linyi in Langye and a nephew of the Grand Tutor Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei, courtesy name Jingxuan, came from Linyi in Langye and was a nephew of Grand Tutor Hong.

sentences.zh: 父孺，光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His father Ru was Grand Master for the Glorious Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ru had been grand master for the glorious chariots.

sentences.zh: 微少好學，無不通覽，善屬文，能書畫，兼解音律、醫方、陰陽術數。

translations.literal: Wei from youth loved learning and left nothing unread; he was skilled at literary composition, could write and paint, and was also versed in music, medicine, and the arts of yin-yang and numerology.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Wei loved learning and read widely; he wrote well, painted skillfully, and was also versed in music, medicine, and the arts of yin-yang and numerology.

sentences.zh: 年十六，州舉秀才，衡陽王義季右軍參軍，並不就。

translations.literal: At sixteen the province recommended him as a cultivated talent, and he was made an aide in the Right Army of the Prince of Hengyang Liu Yiji, but he took neither post.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen the province recommended him as cultivated talent and appointed him aide in Prince Hengyang Liu Yiji's right-army staff, but he accepted neither post.

sentences.zh: 起家司徒祭酒，轉主簿，始興王濬後軍功曹記室參軍，太子中舍人，始興王友。

translations.literal: He began his career as Libationer of the Minister of Works, was transferred to chief clerk, then Merit Officer and Recording Secretary Aide on the Rear Army staff of the Prince of Shixing Liu Jun, Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Friend to the Prince of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as libationer of the minister of works, then chief clerk, then merit officer and recording secretary on Prince Shixing Liu Jun's rear-army staff, gentleman attendant of the heir apparent, and friend to Prince Shixing.

sentences.zh: 父憂去官，服闋，除南平王鑠右軍諮議參軍。

translations.literal: On his father's death he left office; when mourning was finished he was appointed Adviser to the Right Army of the Prince of Nanping Liu Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: He left office on his father's death; when mourning ended he was appointed adviser on Prince Nanping Liu Shuo's right-army staff.

sentences.zh: 微素無宦情，稱疾不就。

translations.literal: Wei had never had a taste for office and pleaded illness without taking the post.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had never cared for office and pleaded illness without accepting.

sentences.zh: 仍除中書侍郎，又擬南琅邪、義興太守，並固辭。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat, and was also nominated Administrator of Southern Langye and of Yixing, but firmly declined all.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed gentleman of the secretariat and also nominated administrator of Southern Langye and of Yixing, but firmly declined every post.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書江湛舉微為吏部郎，微與湛書曰：

translations.literal: Jiang Zhan, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, recommended Wei as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel; Wei wrote to Zhan, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhan, minister of personnel, recommended Wei for gentleman of the ministry of personnel; Wei wrote to Zhan:

sentences.zh: 弟心病亂度，非但蹇蹙而已，此處朝野所共知。

translations.literal: Your younger brother's heart ailment has reached a chaotic degree—not merely lameness and constriction; this is known alike at court and in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Your younger brother's heart ailment has grown chaotic—not merely lameness and constraint; this is known alike at court and in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 騶會忽扣蓽門，閭里咸以為祥怪，君多識前世之載，天值何其易傾。

translations.literal: A mounted messenger suddenly knocked at my humble gate; neighbors all took it for an omen strange or auspicious; you are well versed in records of former ages—how easily Heaven's appointments topple.
translations.idiomatic: A mounted messenger suddenly knocked at my humble gate; the neighbors all took it for an omen, strange or auspicious; you are well read in the records of former ages—how easily Heaven's appointments topple.

sentences.zh: 弟受海內駭笑，不過如燕石禿鶖邪，未知君何以自解於良史邪？

translations.literal: Your younger brother will receive the derisive laughter of the realm—no more than like the Yan stone or the bald stork, is it not? I do not know how you will explain yourself to the good historian.
translations.idiomatic: Your younger brother will become the laughingstock of the realm—no more than the Yan stone or the bald stork, perhaps? I do not know how you will explain yourself to future historians.

sentences.zh: 今雖王道鴻鬯，或有激朗於天表，必欲探援潛寶，傾海求珠，自可卜肆巫祠之間，馬棧牛口之下，賞劇孟於博徒，拔卜式於芻牧。

translations.literal: Though now the royal way is vast and clear, perhaps there are those roused and illumined above the heavens; if you must probe and draw forth hidden treasures and tip the seas to seek pearls, you may well between divination stalls and shaman shrines, beneath horse stalls and ox mouths, reward Ji Meng among gamblers and pull up Bu Shi from fodder and herds.
translations.idiomatic: Though the royal way is now vast and bright, there may yet be men of striking brilliance beyond the common run; if you must hunt hidden talent and drain the seas for pearls, you can find them between fortune-tellers' stalls and shaman shrines, in stables and cattle pens—reward a Ji Meng among gamblers, raise a Bu Shi from the pasture.

sentences.zh: 亦有西戎孤臣，東都戒士，上窮範馳之御，下盡詭遇之能，兼鱗雜襲者，必不乏於世矣。

translations.literal: There are also lone retainers of the western borderlands and guardsmen of the eastern capital, exhausting at the top Fan Chi's driving skill and at the bottom the cunning of opportunistic encounters; those of mixed scales in tangled shoals—surely they are not wanting in the world.
translations.idiomatic: There are also lone retainers from the western marches and seasoned men of the eastern capital—masters of charioteering to the heights of Fan Chi's art, adepts of artful gambits to the depths of crafty encounter; men of many gifts in confused profusion are scarcely rare in this world.

sentences.zh: 且廬於承明，署乎金馬，皆明察之官，又賢於管庫之末。

translations.literal: Moreover, to lodge in Chenming and to be posted at Golden Horse are all offices of clear discernment, and again worthier than the lowest keeper of stores.
translations.idiomatic: Posts at the Chenming Gate and the Golden Horse Gate are offices of keen discernment—far worthier than a humble warehouse clerk.

sentences.zh: 何為劫勒通家疾病人，塵穢難堪之選，將以靖國，不亦益囂乎？

translations.literal: Why coerce and press a chronic invalid from a family intimate with yours—a choice filthy and unbearable—to settle the state? Would it not only make the clamor worse?
translations.idiomatic: Why dragoon a sick neighbor from an old friend of your house—someone filthy and unbearable—as a choice to settle the realm? Would that not only make the scandal worse?

sentences.zh: 《書》云：「任官維賢才」。

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "In appointing office, take talent and worth as the standard."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "In appointing office, look only to talent and worth."

sentences.zh: 而君擢士先疹廢，芃芃棫樸，似不如此。

translations.literal: Yet you promote scholars while putting first the rashly ruined; lush, lush the elm saplings—this seems not to be so.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you raise men while putting first the rashly ruined; "lush are the elm saplings"—surely it cannot mean this.

sentences.zh: 且弟曠違兄姊，迄將十載，姊時歸來，終不任輿曳入閣，兄守金城，永不堪扶抱就路，若不憊疾，非性僻而何。

translations.literal: Moreover your younger brother has kept apart from elder brothers and sisters for nearly ten years; when my sister returns home, I simply cannot bear the carriage being dragged into the gate; my elder brother guards Jincheng and could never endure being helped and carried on the road—if this is not exhaustion from illness, what else could it be but an eccentric nature?
translations.idiomatic: Your younger brother has lived apart from his siblings for nearly ten years; when my sister visits, I cannot even endure being hauled in a carriage through the gate; my elder brother holds Jincheng and could never bear being helped on the road—if this is not illness and exhaustion, what is it but a contrary nature?

sentences.zh: 比君曰表裏，無假長目飛耳也。

translations.literal: Now you speak of inside and outside, but there is no need to borrow long eyes and flying ears.
translations.idiomatic: You speak as though you know me through and through—there is no need to spy with distant eyes and floating ears.

sentences.zh: 常謂生遭太公，將即華士之戮；

translations.literal: I have often said that meeting Lord Grandfather in birth would soon bring Hua Shi's punishment;
translations.idiomatic: I have often said that meeting Taigong in life would soon mean Hua Shi's punishment—

sentences.zh: 幸遇管叔，必蒙僻儒之養。

translations.literal: if fortunately meeting Guan Shu, one would surely receive the fostering of a secluded scholar.
translations.idiomatic: but to meet Guan Shu would mean shelter from a reclusive scholar.

sentences.zh: 光武以馮衍才浮其實，故棄而不齒。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu held that Feng Yan's talent exceeded his substance, and therefore cast him aside and would not rank him among his men.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu found Feng Yan's talent exceeded his substance and cast him aside, refusing to rank him among his men.

sentences.zh: 諸葛孔明云：「來敏亂郡，過於孔文舉。

translations.literal: Zhuge Kongming said: "Lai Min threw counties into chaos, surpassing Kong Wenju.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang said, "Lai Min threw counties into chaos, worse than Kong Rong.

sentences.zh: 」況無古人之才槩，敢干周、漢之常刑。

translations.literal: How much more when one lacks the ancients' caliber of talent and dares to touch the standing punishments of Zhou and Han!
translations.idiomatic: How much more when one lacks the caliber of the ancients and dares to invite the ordinary penalties of Zhou and Han!

sentences.zh: 彼二三英賢，足為曉治與否？

translations.literal: Are those two or three heroic worthies enough to show whether one understands governance?
translations.idiomatic: Are those two or three heroic worthies enough to prove whether one understands governance?

sentences.zh: 恐君逄此時，或亦不免高閣，乃復假名不知己者，豈欲自比衛賜邪？

translations.literal: I fear when you meet this season you too may not escape the high cabinet—and then you again borrow the name of one who does not know you; do you wish to compare yourself to Wei Ci?
translations.idiomatic: I fear when you meet such a time you too may not escape the high cabinet—yet you again borrow the name of one who does not know you; do you wish to compare yourself to Wei Ci?

sentences.zh: 君欲高斅山公，而以仲容見處，徒以搥提禮學，本不參選，鄙夫瞻彼，固不任下走，未知新沓何如州陵耳。

translations.literal: You wish to elevate yourself above Shan Gong, yet treat me as Zhongrong—merely because you hammer at ritual studies, you were never in the candidacies; this vulgar fellow looking at that—surely cannot serve as a runner; I do not know how Xinta compares to Zhouling.
translations.idiomatic: You wish to rank yourself above Shan Tao, yet treat me like Ruan Zhongrong—merely because you hammer at ritual studies, you were never in the candidacies; a vulgar fellow like me, looking at that, surely cannot serve as a runner; I do not know how Xinta measures up to Zhouling.

sentences.zh: 而作不師古，坐亂官政，誣飾蚯蚓，冀招神龍，如復託以真素者，又不宜居華留名，有害風俗。

translations.literal: Yet to act without taking antiquity as teacher, to sit and disorder official government, to adorn earthworms falsely hoping to summon divine dragons—if again one entrusts with unadorned genuineness, one also should not dwell in splendor and leave a name, harming custom.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to act without learning from antiquity, to sit and disorder official government, to dress up earthworms hoping to summon dragons—if you again rely on unadorned genuineness, you also should not dwell in splendor and leave a name, harming public morals.

sentences.zh: 君亦不至期人如此，若交以為人賜，舉未以己勞，則商販之事，又連所不忍聞也。

translations.literal: You also would not expect people so; if friendship becomes men's gifts, and promotion comes from one's own toil—then the affairs of merchants again link to what one cannot bear to hear.
translations.idiomatic: You would not expect this of others either; if friendship becomes a gift from others, and promotion comes from one's own labor—then the ways of merchants touch what I cannot bear to hear.

sentences.zh: 豈謂不肖易擢，貪者可誘，凡此數者，君必居一焉。

translations.literal: Can it be said that the unworthy are easy to promote and the greedy can be lured? Among all these several, you must occupy one.
translations.idiomatic: Do you mean that the unworthy are easy to promote and the greedy can be tempted? Among these several, you must be one.

sentences.zh: 雖假天口於齊駢，藉鬼說於周季，公孫碎毛髮之文，莊生縱漭瀁之極，終不能舉其契，為之辭矣。

translations.literal: Even if borrowing Heaven's mouth from Qi Pian, borrowing ghost speech from Zhou Ji, Gongsun Sun's hair-splitting prose, and Zhuangzi's utmost of vast flood—all cannot lift their contract; I have made my excuse.
translations.idiomatic: Even if you borrowed Heaven's mouth from Qi Pian, ghost speech from Zhou Ji, Gongsun Long's hair-splitting prose, and Zhuangzi's utmost flood of words—you still could not fulfill their bargain; I have said my piece.

sentences.zh: 子將明魂，必靈咍於萬里，汝、潁餘彥，將拂衣而不朝。

translations.literal: Your enlightened souls will surely wail in spirit beyond ten thousand li; the remaining fine men of Ru and Ying will dust their robes and not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: The enlightened dead will surely wail in spirit across ten thousand li; the remaining fine men of Ru and Ying will shake out their robes and refuse court.

sentences.zh: 浮華一開，風俗或從此而爽。

translations.literal: Once vain show opens, custom may from this slip away.
translations.idiomatic: Once vain display is unleashed, public morals may slip away from this.

sentences.zh: 鬼谷以揣情為最難，何君忖度之輕謬。

translations.literal: Guigu regarded fathoming emotion as most difficult—why is your lordship's weighing so light and mistaken?
translations.idiomatic: Guiguzi held that reading another's feelings was the hardest thing—why is your judgment so light and mistaken?

sentences.zh: 今有此書，非敢叨擬中散，誠不能顧影負心，純盜虛聲，所以綿絡累紙，本不營尚書虎爪板也。

translations.literal: Now having this letter—I do not dare presumptuously to compare myself to Zhongsan; truly I cannot look at my shadow and betray my heart, purely stealing empty reputation—therefore I string together and pile up sheets; originally I do not scheme for the Secretariat's tiger-claw board.
translations.idiomatic: This letter is not written because I dare compare myself to Ji Kang; I truly cannot face my reflection and betray my heart, stealing only empty fame—hence these piled sheets. I never sought the Secretariat's tiger-claw board in the first place.

sentences.zh: 成童便往來居舍，晨省復經周旋，加有諸甥，亦何得頓絕慶弔。

translations.literal: From attaining childhood I have gone back and forth to the residence; morning attendance again passes through dealings; adding the various nephews—how could I suddenly cut off congratulations and mourning?
translations.idiomatic: Since childhood I have visited the household back and forth; morning calls and daily courtesies continue, and with all the nephews besides—how could I suddenly cut off congratulations and condolences?

sentences.zh: 然生平之意，自於此都盡。

translations.literal: Yet the meaning of a lifetime—from this it is all exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the purpose of my life ends here entirely.

sentences.zh: 君平公云：「生我名者殺我身。

translations.literal: Lord Ping said: "Those who give me a name will kill my body.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Ping of Jun said, "Those who give me a name will kill my body.

sentences.zh: 」天爵且猶滅名，安用吏部郎哉！

translations.literal: " Even heavenly rank still extinguishes one's name—what use is Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel!
translations.idiomatic: " Even heavenly rank still destroys one's name—what use is gentleman of the ministry of personnel!

sentences.zh: 其舉可陋，其事不經，非獨搢紳者不道，僕妾皆將咲之。

translations.literal: This recommendation is contemptible; the affair is unorthodox—not only will gentry not speak of it; servants and concubines too will laugh.
translations.idiomatic: This recommendation is base; the affair is irregular—not only will the gentry refuse to discuss it; even servants and concubines will laugh.

sentences.zh: 忽忽不樂，自知壽不得長，且使千載知弟不詐諼耳。

translations.literal: Distracted and unhappy, I know my life cannot be long—at least let a thousand years know your younger brother does not feign illness.
translations.idiomatic: Restless and unhappy, I know I cannot live long—at least let posterity know your younger brother does not sham illness.

sentences.zh: 微既為始興王濬府吏，濬數相存慰，微奉答箋書，輒飾以辭采。

translations.literal: Wei, having become a clerk in Prince Shixing Liu Jun's household, Jun often visited to console him; Wei in reply memorial letters always adorned them with literary color.
translations.idiomatic: Wei served as clerk in Prince Shixing Liu Jun's household; the prince often called on him in consolation, and Wei dressed his replies in fine literary ornament.

sentences.zh: 微為文古甚，頗抑揚，袁淑見之，謂為訴屈。

translations.literal: Wei's writing was very archaic in style, with considerable modulation; Yuan Shu on seeing it said it was pleading grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's prose was heavily archaizing and modulated; Yuan Shu, on reading it, said it sounded like a plea of wrongs suffered.

sentences.zh: 微因此又與從弟僧綽書曰：

translations.literal: Wei therefore again wrote to his cousin Sengchuo, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Wei therefore wrote again to his cousin Sengchuo:

sentences.zh: 吾雖無人鑒，要是早知弟，每共宴語，前言何嘗不以止足為貴。

translations.literal: Though I have no mirror of men, I did know you early; whenever we feasted and talked, did I not always take knowing when to stop as precious?
translations.idiomatic: Though I lack the eye to judge men, I have known you long; whenever we feasted and talked, did I not always prize knowing when to stop?

sentences.zh: 且持盈畏滿，自是家門舊風，何為一旦落漠至此，當局苦迷，將不然邪！

translations.literal: Moreover, holding fullness in fear and dreading excess is our family's old way—why fall into such desolation at once? Those in office are painfully blind—will it not prove so!
translations.idiomatic: Holding fullness in fear and dreading excess is our family's old way—why plunge into such desolation at once? Those in power are painfully blind—will it not prove so!

sentences.zh: 詎容都不先聞，或可不知耳。

translations.literal: How could you not have heard first—perhaps you truly did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Could you really not have heard beforehand—or perhaps you truly did not know.

sentences.zh: 衣冠胄胤，如吾者甚多，才能固不足道，唯不傾側溢詐，士頗以此容之。

translations.literal: Scions of hat and gown like me are many; talent is indeed not worth mentioning—only that I do not lean and overflow in deceit; gentlemen are somewhat tolerant on that account.
translations.idiomatic: There are many scions of hat and gown like me; my talent is hardly worth mentioning—only that I do not lean and overflow in deceit; gentlemen are somewhat tolerant of that.

sentences.zh: 至於規矩細行，難可詳料。

translations.literal: As for rules and fine conduct, it is hard to reckon in detail.
translations.idiomatic: As for propriety in small matters, it is hard to reckon in detail.

sentences.zh: 疹疾日滋，縱恣益甚，人道所貴，廢不復脩。

translations.literal: Rash illness grows daily; wantonness grows worse; what human conduct esteems, I have abandoned and no longer cultivate.
translations.idiomatic: My rash illness grows daily; my wantonness grows worse; what human conduct esteems, I have abandoned and no longer cultivate.

sentences.zh: 幸值聖明相容，置之教外，且舊恩所及，每蒙寬假。

translations.literal: Fortunately the sage brightness tolerates me, placing me outside instruction, and the old favor I have received wins repeated indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately the sage court tolerates me, placing me outside instruction, and old favors win me repeated indulgence.

sentences.zh: 吾亦自揆疾疹重侵，難復支振，民生安樂之事，心死久矣。

translations.literal: I too judge that my rash illness has deeply invaded and I can hardly support myself; the affairs of human joy and ease—the heart died of them long ago.
translations.idiomatic: I too see that my rash illness has deeply invaded and I can hardly hold up; the pleasures of human life—my heart died to them long ago.

sentences.zh: 所以解日偷存，盡於大布糲粟，半夕安寢，便以自度，血氣盈虛，不復稍道，長以大散為和羹，弟為不見之邪？

translations.literal: Therefore I steal days to survive, limiting myself to coarse cloth and coarse grain; half a night of peaceful sleep I take as my measure; the fullness and emptiness of blood and breath I no longer discuss at all; long I have taken great powder as harmonizing broth—does my younger brother not see this?
translations.idiomatic: So I steal days to survive on coarse cloth and coarse grain; half a night's sleep is my measure; I no longer speak of the ebb and flow of my vital forces; for long I have taken powdered drugs as my daily broth—does my younger brother not see this?

sentences.zh: 疾廢居然，且事一己，上不足敗俗傷化，下不至毀辱家門，泊爾尸居，無方待化。

translations.literal: Illness and ruin are settled; I attend only to myself—above, not enough to harm custom and wound transformation; below, not reaching to disgrace the family gate; placidly I dwell like a corpse, with no method awaiting change.
translations.idiomatic: My illness has reduced me to this; I mind only myself—above, not enough to harm public morals; below, not enough to disgrace the family; I live like a corpse, awaiting nothing.

sentences.zh: 凡此二三，皆是事實。

translations.literal: All these two or three are facts.
translations.idiomatic: All these two or three points are facts.

sentences.zh: 吾與弟書，不得家中相欺也。

translations.literal: In letters to my younger brother I cannot deceive within the family.
translations.idiomatic: In writing to you I cannot deceive within the family.

sentences.zh: 州陵此舉，為無所因，反覆思之，了不能解。

translations.literal: Zhouling's act has no cause whatsoever; turning it over in thought, I cannot understand it at all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouling's act has no cause I can see; turning it over in thought, I cannot understand it at all.

sentences.zh: 豈見吾近者諸牋邪，良可怪笑。

translations.literal: Did he see my recent memorials? They are truly laughable.
translations.idiomatic: Did he see my recent memorials? They are truly laughable.

sentences.zh: 吾少學作文，又晚節如小進，使君公欲民不偷，每加存飾，酬對尊貴，不厭敬恭。

translations.literal: I studied composition young, and in late years made a small advance; when lord and prince wished the people not to be remiss, he always added polish; in answering the honored and noble I am not weary of respect.
translations.idiomatic: I studied writing young, and in later years made a small advance; when the prince wished the people not to be remiss, he always added polish; in answering the great I am not weary of respect.

sentences.zh: 且文詞不怨思抑揚，則流澹無味。

translations.literal: Moreover, if literary words lack grievous thought and modulation, they flow thin and without flavor.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, if literary words lack grievous thought and modulation, they flow thin and tasteless.

sentences.zh: 文好古，貴能連類可悲，一往視之，如似多意。

translations.literal: Writing that esteems antiquity values being able to link categories in moving grief; on first reading it seems to carry much meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Writing that esteems antiquity values linking themes in moving grief; at first glance it seems to carry much meaning.

sentences.zh: 當見居非求志，清論所排，便是通辭訴屈邪。

translations.literal: When one sees that dwelling is not seeking office, what the pure discussants reject—is that then general language pleading grievance?
translations.idiomatic: When one sees that staying home is not seeking office, what the pure discussants reject—is that pleading grievance in general terms?

sentences.zh: 爾者真可謂真素寡矣！

translations.literal: That sort can truly be called scant in unadorned genuineness!
translations.idiomatic: That can truly be called scant in unadorned genuineness!

sentences.zh: 其數旦見客小防，自來盈門，亦不煩獨舉吉也。

translations.literal: The number of times I see guests on small guard—when they come of themselves the gate is full—I also do not trouble to raise auspicious signs alone.
translations.idiomatic: I see guests on small guard now and then—when they come of themselves my gate is full—I do not trouble to raise auspicious signs alone.

sentences.zh: 此輩乃云語勢所至，非其要也。

translations.literal: These people say it is where the tone of speech arrives—not their main point.
translations.idiomatic: These people say it is where the tone of speech leads—not their main point.

sentences.zh: 弟無懷居今地，萬物初不以相非，然魯器齊虛，實宜書紳。

translations.literal: My younger brother need not dwell on this place today; at first all things do not reject one another—yet when Lu vessels are empty in Qi, it truly should be written on the sash.
translations.idiomatic: You need not dwell on this place today; at first all things do not reject one another—yet when Lu vessels are empty in Qi, it truly should be written on the sash.

sentences.zh: 今三署六府之人，誰表裏此內，儻疑弟豫有力，於素論何如哉。

translations.literal: Now among the people of the Three Offices and Six Ministries, who shows inside and outside on this? If perchance they suspect my younger brother has hidden strength, what of that to plain discussion?
translations.idiomatic: Now among the people of the Three Offices and Six Ministries, who shows inside and outside on this? If they suspect you have hidden influence, what does that matter to plain discussion?

sentences.zh: 則吾長阨不死，終誤盛壯也。

translations.literal: Then I will long be blocked undying and in the end mislead my prime of life.
translations.idiomatic: Then I will long be blocked undying and in the end mislead my prime of life.

sentences.zh: 江不過強吹拂吾，云是巖穴人。

translations.literal: Jiang merely forced a strong puff at me, saying I am a cave-dweller.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang merely blew hard at me, saying I am a cave-dweller.

sentences.zh: 巖穴人情所高，吾得當此，則雞鶩變作鳳皇，何為干飾廉隅，秩秩見於面目，所惜者大耳。

translations.literal: Cave-dwellers are what sentiment esteems; if I receive this, then chickens and ducks change into phoenixes—why bother to adorn clean corners, appearing orderly in face? What one regrets is the great matter.
translations.idiomatic: Cave-dwellers are what the age esteems; if I receive this label, chickens and ducks turn into phoenixes—why bother to polish clean corners and look orderly in the face? What one regrets is the larger matter.

sentences.zh: 諸舍闔門皆蒙時私，此既未易陳道，故常因含聲不言。

translations.literal: All the households of the clan receive private favor from the times; this is not easy to state, so I often swallow my voice and do not speak.
translations.idiomatic: All our clan households receive private favor from the times; this is not easy to state, so I often keep silent.

sentences.zh: 至兄弟，尤為叨竊，臨海頻煩二郡，謙亦越進清階，吾高枕家巷，遂至中書郎，此足以闔棺矣。

translations.literal: As for brothers, the favor is especially excessive: Linhai repeatedly asked for two commanderies; Qian also overstepped into clear ranks; I rested high on a pillow in the home lane and reached Gentleman of the Secretariat—this is enough to close the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: As for brothers, the favor is especially excessive: Linhai repeatedly held two commanderies; Qian also rose beyond his due into clear ranks; I rested at home and reached gentleman of the secretariat—this is enough to close the coffin.

sentences.zh: 又前年優旨，自弟所宣，雖夏后撫辜人，周宣及鰥寡，不足過也。

translations.literal: Moreover last year's gracious edict was proclaimed by my younger brother; though Yu the Great comforted the guilty and King Xuan reached widows and orphans, it does not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover last year's gracious edict was proclaimed by you; though Yu comforted the guilty and King Xuan reached widows and orphans, it does not surpass this.

sentences.zh: 語皆循檢校跡，不為虛飾也。

translations.literal: The words all follow inspection and verification of traces—not empty adornment.
translations.idiomatic: The words all follow what can be inspected and verified—not empty adornment.

sentences.zh: 作人不阿諛，無緣頭髮見白，稍學諂詐。

translations.literal: In conduct I do not flatter; without cause hair on the head turns white—I have not slightly learned flattery and deceit.
translations.idiomatic: In conduct I do not flatter; without cause my hair has turned white—I have not slightly learned flattery and deceit.

sentences.zh: 且吾何以為，足不能行，自不得出戶；

translations.literal: Moreover what am I fit for? My feet cannot walk, so of myself I cannot leave the door;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover what am I fit for? My feet cannot walk, so I cannot leave the door;

sentences.zh: 頭不耐風，故不可扶曳。

translations.literal: my head cannot bear wind, so I cannot be helped and dragged along.
translations.idiomatic: my head cannot bear wind, so I cannot be helped and dragged along.

sentences.zh: 家本貧餧，至於惡衣蔬食，設使盜蹠居此，亦不能兩展其足，妄意珍藏也。

translations.literal: The family was originally poor and hungry; as for bad clothes and coarse food—even if Robber Zhi lived here, he could not stretch both feet twice and vainly think of hoarding treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Our family was always poor and hungry, down to bad clothes and coarse food—even if Robber Zhi lived here, he could not stretch both feet twice and dream of hoarding treasure.

sentences.zh: 正令選官設作此舉，於吾亦無劍戟之傷，所以懃懃畏人之多言也。

translations.literal: Even if the selection office set up this act, for me there is no wound of sword or halberd; therefore I am earnest in fearing many people's talk.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the selection office set up this act, it would not wound me with sword or halberd; what I earnestly fear is many people's talk.

sentences.zh: 管子晉賢，乃關人主之輕重，此何容易哉。

translations.literal: Guanzi was a Jin worthy, yet it concerned the ruler's weight and lightness—this is not easy!
translations.idiomatic: Guanzi was a worthy of Jin, yet it bore on the ruler's weight and lightness—this is no easy matter!

sentences.zh: 州陵亦自言視明聽聰，而返區區飾吾，何辯致而下英俊。

translations.literal: Zhouling also says himself that his sight is clear and hearing sharp, yet in return he minutely adorns me—how does he argue down and yield to heroic worthies?
translations.idiomatic: Zhouling also says his sight is clear and hearing sharp, yet in return he fusses over adorning me—how does he argue down and yield to heroic worthies?

sentences.zh: 夫奇士必龍居深藏，與蛙蝦為伍，放勳其猶難之，林宗輩不足識也。

translations.literal: A strange scholar must dwell hidden like a dragon, in the company of frogs and shrimp; even Emperor Yao found it hard; men of Linzong's sort are not enough to know him.
translations.idiomatic: A strange scholar must dwell hidden like a dragon, among frogs and shrimp; even Emperor Yao found it hard; men of Guo Linzong's sort are not enough to know him.

sentences.zh: 似不肯睠睠奉牋記，雕琢獻文章，居家近市廛，親戚滿城府，吾猶自知袁陽源輩當平此不？

translations.literal: As if unwilling to look back and offer memorials, carving and polishing to present essays, dwelling near the market, relatives filling the city offices—I still know myself whether Yuan Yangyuan's sort would level this or not?
translations.idiomatic: As if unwilling to look back and offer memorials, carving essays to present, dwelling near the market with relatives filling the city offices—I still know whether Yuan Yangyuan's sort would level this or not?

sentences.zh: 飾詐之與直獨，兩不關吾心，又何所耿介。

translations.literal: Adorning deceit and standing alone in genuineness—the two do not touch my heart; what is there to be upright and obstructive about?
translations.idiomatic: Adorning deceit and standing alone in genuineness—neither touches my heart; what is there to be stiff about?

sentences.zh: 弟自宜以解塞群賢矣，兼悉怒此言自爾家任兄故能也。

translations.literal: My younger brother should himself use this to block the crowd of worthies; I also know that angry words come from your family's elder brother Ren's ability.
translations.idiomatic: You should yourself use this to answer the crowd of worthies; I also know angry words come from your family's elder brother Ren's ability.

sentences.zh: 日日望弟來，屬病終不起，何意向與江書，粗布胸心，無人可寫，比面乃具與弟。

translations.literal: Day by day I hoped my younger brother would come; entrusted with illness I ultimately could not rise—what intent in writing to Jiang, roughly laying out the heart, no one to write for; only on meeting face to face did I fully give it to my younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Day by day I hoped you would come; entrusted with illness I ultimately could not rise—my intent in writing to Jiang was roughly to lay out my heart; there was no one to write for me; only when we met face to face did I give it fully to you.

sentences.zh: 書便覺成，本以當半日相見，吾既惡勞，不得多語，樞機幸非所長，相見亦不勝讀此書也。

translations.literal: The letter was then felt complete; originally it was to meet half a day—I hate labor and cannot speak much; pivots and keys are fortunately not my strength; meeting also cannot surpass reading this letter.
translations.idiomatic: The letter then felt complete; originally we were to meet half a day—I hate exertion and cannot speak much; pivots and keys are not my strength; meeting would not surpass reading this letter.

sentences.zh: 親屬欲見自可示，無急付手。

translations.literal: If kinsmen wish to see it they may be shown; no need urgently to hand it over.
translations.idiomatic: If kinsmen wish to see it they may be shown; no need to hand it over in haste.

sentences.zh: 時論者或云微之見舉，廬江何偃亦豫其議，慮為微所咎，與書自陳。

translations.literal: At the time some in discussion said that Wei's being recommended—He Yan of Lujiang also took part in the deliberation—and feared being blamed by Wei, and wrote to explain himself.
translations.idiomatic: At the time some said that in Wei's recommendation He Yan of Lujiang also took part in the deliberation, feared Wei would blame him, and wrote to explain himself.

sentences.zh: 微報之曰：

translations.literal: Wei replied to him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Wei replied to him:

sentences.zh: 卿昔稱吾於義興，吾常謂之見知，然復自怪鄙野，不參風流，未有一介熟悉於事，何用獨識之也。

translations.literal: You once praised me at Yixing; I always called that being known—yet again I wondered at my own rustic wildness, not joining the current, not having a single acquaintance familiar in affairs—why use unique knowledge of me?
translations.idiomatic: You once praised me at Yixing; I always called that being known—yet I also wondered at my rustic wildness, not joining the current, not having a single acquaintance versed in affairs—why single me out for special knowledge?

sentences.zh: 近日何見綽送卿書，雖知如戲，知卿固不能相哀。

translations.literal: Recently I saw Chuo send your letter; though I know it as if in jest, I know you truly cannot pity me.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I saw Sengchuo send your letter; though I know it as if in jest, I know you truly cannot pity me.

sentences.zh: 苟相哀之未知，何相期之可論。

translations.literal: If pity is not yet known, how can expectation be discussed?
translations.idiomatic: If pity is not yet known, how can expectation be discussed?

sentences.zh: 卿少陶玄風，淹雅脩暢，自是正始中人。

translations.literal: You young steeped in the dark wind, refined and elegant in cultivation and fluency—of yourself a man of the Zhengshi era.
translations.idiomatic: You young steeped in the Zhengshi style, refined and fluent—by nature a man of the Zhengshi era.

sentences.zh: 吾真庸性人耳，自然志操不倍王、樂。

translations.literal: I am truly a man of vulgar nature; my natural resolve and conduct do not double Wang and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: I am truly a vulgar nature; my natural resolve and conduct do not double Wang Rong and Yue Guang.

sentences.zh: 小兒時尤麤笨無好，常從博士讀小小章句，竟無可得，口吃不能劇讀，遂絕意於尋求。

translations.literal: In small childhood I was especially coarse and stupid without excellence; I always followed the Erudite reading small chapter-and-sentence texts—ultimately nothing obtained; stammering, unable to read aloud forcefully, I then cut off intent in seeking.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood I was especially coarse and dull; I always followed the Erudite reading minor chapter-and-sentence texts—ultimately I gained nothing; stammering, unable to read aloud forcefully, I then gave up seeking learning.

sentences.zh: 至二十左右，方復就觀小說，往來者見床頭有數帙書，便言學問，試就檢，當何有哉。

translations.literal: Around twenty I again drew near to reading minor tales; those coming and going saw several bundles of books at the head of the bed and said I studied—try inspecting them: what could there be?
translations.idiomatic: Around twenty I again drew near to reading minor tales; visitors saw several bundles of books at my bedside and said I studied—try inspecting them: what could there be?

sentences.zh: 乃復持此擬議人邪。

translations.literal: Yet again you hold this to discuss people?
translations.idiomatic: Yet again you hold this to judge people?

sentences.zh: 尚獨愧咲揚子之褒贍，猶恥辭賦為君子，若吾篆刻，菲亦甚矣。

translations.literal: I alone am ashamed to laugh at Yangzi's praise and bounty, yet also ashamed to take ci-fu as a gentleman's work; if my seal-carving is base, it is also very much so.
translations.idiomatic: I alone am ashamed to laugh at Yang Xiong's praise and bounty, yet also ashamed to take rhapsodies as a gentleman's work; if my seal-carving is base, it is very base indeed.

sentences.zh: 卿諸人亦當尤以此見議。

translations.literal: You gentlemen too should especially blame me on this account.
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen too should especially blame me on this account.

sentences.zh: 或謂言深博，作一段意氣，鄙薄人世，初不敢然。

translations.literal: Some say the words are deep and broad, putting on a stretch of spirit, despising and slighting the human world—I at first did not dare so.
translations.idiomatic: Some say my words are deep and broad, putting on a stretch of spirit, despising the human world—I at first did not dare so.

sentences.zh: 是以每見世人文賦書論，無所是非，不解處即日借問，此其本心也。

translations.literal: Therefore whenever I see the world's literary rhapsodies, essays, and treatises, I have no yes or no; where I do not understand I borrow and ask the same day—this is my true heart.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore whenever I see the world's literary rhapsodies, essays, and treatises, I have no yes or no; where I do not understand I ask the same day—this is my true heart.

sentences.zh: 至於生平好服上藥，起年十二時病虛耳。

translations.literal: As for lifelong fondness for taking superior drugs, it began when at twelve I was ill and weak.
translations.idiomatic: As for lifelong fondness for taking superior drugs, it began when at twelve I was ill and weak.

sentences.zh: 所撰服食方中，粗言之矣。

translations.literal: In the ingestion formulas I compiled, I have spoken of them roughly.
translations.idiomatic: In the ingestion formulas I compiled, I have spoken of them roughly.

sentences.zh: 自此始信攝養有徵，故門冬昌朮，隨時參進。

translations.literal: From this I first believed that regulated nourishment had effect; therefore winter asparagus and atractylodes I take in season as they come.
translations.idiomatic: From this I first believed regulated nourishment had effect; therefore winter asparagus and atractylodes I take in season as they come.

sentences.zh: 寒溫相補，欲以扶護危羸，見冀白首。

translations.literal: Cold and warmth complement each other, intending to support and protect the dangerously frail, hoping to see white hair.
translations.idiomatic: Cold and warmth complement each other, intending to support my dangerously frail body, hoping to see white hair.

sentences.zh: 家貧乏役，至於春秋令節，輒自將兩三門生，入草采之。

translations.literal: The family is poor and lacks servants; even at the seasonal festivals of spring and autumn I myself take two or three disciples into the grass to gather them.
translations.idiomatic: The family is poor and lacks servants; even at the seasonal festivals of spring and autumn I myself take two or three disciples into the grass to gather them.

sentences.zh: 吾實倦遊醫部，頗曉和藥，尤信《本草》，欲其必行，是以躬親，意在取精。

translations.literal: I truly weary of wandering the medical departments, yet am quite versed in compounding drugs, especially trusting the Materia Medica, wishing it must be effective—therefore I personally attend, intent on taking the essence.
translations.idiomatic: I truly weary of wandering the medical departments, yet am quite versed in compounding drugs, especially trusting the Materia Medica, wishing it must be effective—therefore I personally attend, intent on taking the essence.

sentences.zh: 世人便言希仙好異，矯慕不羈，不同家頗有罵之者。

translations.literal: The world then says I desire immortals and love the strange, admire and imitate unconstraint—unlike my family, there are quite a few who revile me.
translations.idiomatic: The world then says I desire immortals and love the strange, admire and imitate unconstraint—unlike my family, quite a few revile me for it.

sentences.zh: 又性知畫繢，蓋亦鳴鵠識夜之機，盤紆糾紛，或記心目，故兼山水之愛，一往跡求，皆仿像也。

translations.literal: Moreover by nature I know painting; it is also the mechanism by which the calling goose knows night; coiled and tangled, confused and knotted, sometimes I record in mind and eye—therefore I also love mountains and waters; going once to seek traces, all are imitations.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover by nature I know painting; it is also the mechanism by which the calling goose knows night; coiled and tangled in mind and eye—therefore I also love mountains and waters; going once to seek traces, all are imitations.

sentences.zh: 不好詣人，能忘榮以避權右，宜自密應對舉止，因卷慙自保，不能勉其所短耳。

translations.literal: I do not like calling on people; able to forget glory to avoid the powerful right—I should myself be secret in answering and bearing, and by curling up in shame protect myself—unable to force what is short in me.
translations.idiomatic: I do not like calling on people; able to forget glory to avoid the powerful right—I should myself be secret in answering and bearing, and by curling up in shame protect myself—unable to force what is short in me.

sentences.zh: 由來有此數條，二三諸賢，因復架累，致之高塵，詠之清壑。

translations.literal: From of old there have been these several items; two or three worthies, again piling layer on layer, raised them to high dust, sang them into clear ravines.
translations.idiomatic: From of old there have been these several points about me; two or three worthies have again piled them up, exalted them to lofty heights, and sung them into clear ravines.

sentences.zh: 瓦礫有資，不敢輕廁金銀也。

translations.literal: Tiles and rubble have their use; I dare not lightly use them as toilet with gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Even tiles and rubble have their place; I dare not lightly rank them beside gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 而頃年嬰疾，沉淪無已，區區之情，愒於生存，自恐難復，而先命猥加，魂氣褰薾，常人不得作常自處疾苦，正亦臥思已熟，謂有記自論。

translations.literal: But in recent years I suffer illness, sinking without end; petty feelings wearied at surviving, myself fearing hard recovery, yet fate prematurely imposed, soul-breath drooping weak—ordinary people cannot normally handle their own illness; I too, lying in bed, have thought it through and said there was record of self-discussion.
translations.idiomatic: But in recent years I have been stricken with illness, sinking without end; petty feelings wearied at clinging to life, fearing I might not recover, yet fate has prematurely pressed down and my spirit droops weak—ordinary people cannot normally manage their own illness; lying abed I have thought it through and supposed there was some written self-account.

sentences.zh: 既仰天光，不夭庶類，兼望諸賢，共相哀體，而卿首唱誕言，布之翰墨，萬石之慎，或未然邪。

translations.literal: Having looked up to heaven's light, not dying young among the multitude, also hoping the worthies would together pity my body—yet you first sang wild words, spread them in brush and ink; ten thousand piculs of caution—perhaps not so?
translations.idiomatic: Having received heaven's light and not died young among the multitude, I also hoped the worthies would together pity my condition—yet you first voiced extravagant words and spread them in ink; is the caution of ten thousand piculs perhaps not so after all?

sentences.zh: 好盡之累，豈其如此。

translations.literal: The burden of speaking to the fullest—could it really be so?
translations.idiomatic: The burden of saying everything—could it really be so?

sentences.zh: 綽大駭歎，便是闔朝見病者。

translations.literal: Chuo greatly startled and sighed; then it is the whole court seeing the sick man.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo was greatly startled and sighed; then the whole court sees the sick man.

sentences.zh: 吾本儜人，加疹意惛，一旦聞此，便惶怖矣。

translations.literal: I am originally a poor man; plus rash mind confused—once hearing this, at once terrified.
translations.idiomatic: I am by nature a poor-spirited man; with rash mind confused, once I heard this I was at once terrified.

sentences.zh: 五六日來，復苦心痛，引喉狀如胸中悉腫，甚自憂。

translations.literal: Five or six days now, again suffering heart pain; throat drawn as if the chest were entirely swollen—greatly worried myself.
translations.idiomatic: For five or six days now I have again suffered heart pain; my throat constricts as if my whole chest were swollen—I am deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 力作此答，無復條貫，貴布所懷，落漠不舉。

translations.literal: Forced to make this reply, no more order; value spreading what I harbor—desolate, unable to raise.
translations.idiomatic: I forced myself to write this reply; it has no structure left. I value only laying bare what I harbor—desolate, I cannot lift myself.

sentences.zh: 卿既不可解，立欲便別，且當笑。

translations.literal: You already cannot be understood, immediately want to part—for now you ought to laugh.
translations.idiomatic: You are already beyond understanding and want to leave at once—for now you ought to laugh.

sentences.zh: 微常住門屋一間，尋書玩古，如此者十餘年。

translations.literal: Wei always dwelt in one room at the gate-house, seeking books and enjoying antiquities—thus for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Wei always lived in a single room at the family gate-house, seeking books and enjoying antiquities—thus for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其善筮，賜以名蓍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, because of his skill at divination, bestowed famous yarrow stalks.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, because of his skill at divination, bestowed upon him famous yarrow stalks.

sentences.zh: 弟僧謙，亦有才譽，為太子舍人，遇疾，微躬自處治，而僧謙服藥失度，遂卒。

translations.literal: His younger brother Sengqian also had talent and reputation, served as Crown Prince Attendant; falling ill, Wei personally treated him, but Sengqian took medicine in excess and died.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Sengqian also had talent and reputation and served as Crown Prince Attendant. When he fell ill, Wei personally treated him, but Sengqian took the medicine in excess and died.

sentences.zh: 微深自咎恨，發病不復自治，哀痛僧謙不能已，以書告靈曰：

translations.literal: Wei deeply blamed himself, fell ill and no longer treated himself, grief for Sengqian unceasing, and wrote to inform the spirit, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Wei deeply blamed himself, fell ill and no longer treated himself, and could not cease grieving for Sengqian. He wrote to inform the spirit, saying:

sentences.zh: 弟年十五，始居宿於外，不為察慧之譽，獨沉浮好書，聆琴聞操，輒有過目之能。

translations.literal: My younger brother at fifteen first lodged abroad; he did not win praise for keen insight, but alone drifted in love of books; hearing the qin and its pieces, he at once had ability to remember at a glance.
translations.idiomatic: My brother was fifteen when he first lodged away from home. He won no praise for keen insight, but drifted happily among books; when he heard the qin and its pieces, he remembered them at a glance.

sentences.zh: 討測文典，斟酌傳記，寒暑未交，便卓然可述。

translations.literal: Probing and measuring literary canons, weighing and sifting biographies—before cold and heat had exchanged, he was already outstanding enough to be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: Probing literary canons and weighing biographies—before a season had passed, he was already accomplished enough to be spoken of.

sentences.zh: 吾長病，或有小間，輒稱引前載，不異舊學。

translations.literal: I long ill; whenever there was slight respite, he would cite and draw on former records, no different from old learning.
translations.idiomatic: I have long been ill; whenever I had a slight respite, he would cite former records, no different from a trained scholar.

sentences.zh: 自爾日就月將，著名邦黨，方隆夙志，嗣美前賢，何圖一旦冥然長往，酷痛煩冤，心如焚裂。

translations.literal: From then day by day advancing, month by month rising, famous in the district and clan, about to fulfill his early ambition and continue the beauty of former worthies—who thought that in one morning he would darkly go far away? Cruel pain and vexing grief; my heart like burning and splitting.
translations.idiomatic: From then he advanced day by day and month by month, famous in the district and clan, about to fulfill his early ambition and continue the beauty of former worthies—who thought that one morning he would suddenly go forever? Cruel pain and vexing grief—my heart feels burned and torn apart.

sentences.zh: 尋念平生，裁十年中耳。

translations.literal: Reflecting on our lives together, it is only ten years within.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back on our lives together, it is only ten years at most.

sentences.zh: 然非公事，無不相對，一字之書，必共詠讀；

translations.literal: Yet if not public business, there was nothing we did not face together; a book of one character—we must chant and read it together;
translations.idiomatic: Yet apart from public business, we were never apart; a book of a single character—we had to chant and read it together;

sentences.zh: 一句之文，無不研賞，濁酒忘愁，圖籍相慰，吾所以窮而不憂，實賴此耳。

translations.literal: a text of one line—without fail we studied and savored it; muddy wine to forget sorrow, maps and registers for consolation—my reason for being poor yet not grieving truly relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: a text of a single line—we always studied and savored it together; muddy wine to forget sorrow, maps and books for consolation—the reason I could be poor yet not despair truly lay in this.

sentences.zh: 奈何罪酷，煢然獨坐。

translations.literal: Alas for cruel fate—desolate, I sit alone.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for cruel fate—I sit desolate and alone.

sentences.zh: 憶往年散發，極目流涕，吾不舍日夜，又恆慮吾羸病，豈圖奄忽，先歸冥冥。

translations.literal: I recall in former years letting my hair down, gazing to the limit with streaming tears; I would not leave you day or night, and always feared my frail illness—who thought you would suddenly pass away and go first to the dark?
translations.idiomatic: I recall how in former years you would let your hair down and gaze into the distance with streaming tears; I would not leave you day or night, and always feared for my frail illness—who thought you would suddenly pass away and go first into the dark?

sentences.zh: 反覆萬慮，無復一期，音顏髣髴，觸事歷然，弟今何在，令吾悲窮。

translations.literal: Turning it over ten thousand times in thought, there is no meeting again; voice and face seem near, every matter vividly clear—where is my brother now? It makes my grief endless.
translations.idiomatic: Turning it over ten thousand times in my mind, there is no meeting again; your voice and face seem near, every memory vividly clear—where is my brother now? My grief has no end.

sentences.zh: 昔仕京師，分張六旬耳，其中三過，誤云今日何意不來，鍾念懸心，無物能譬。

translations.literal: In former years serving in the capital, we were apart only sixty days within; among them three times I mistakenly said, 'Why do you not come today?'—heart hung in thought, nothing could compare.
translations.idiomatic: When I served in the capital we were apart only sixty days in all; three times I mistakenly said, 'Why do you not come today?'—my heart hung on you, nothing could compare.

sentences.zh: 方欲共營林澤，以送餘年，念茲有何罪戾，見此夭酷，沒於吾手，觸事痛恨。

translations.literal: We were just about to together plan groves and marshes to send off our remaining years—what guilt is in this thought, to see this untimely cruelty? He perished in my hands; every matter stirs bitter regret.
translations.idiomatic: We were just about to plan groves and marshes together to spend our remaining years—what guilt lay in this wish, to see such untimely cruelty? He perished by my hand; every memory stirs bitter regret.

sentences.zh: 吾素好醫術，不使弟子得全，又尋思不精，致有枉過，念此一條，特復痛酷。
