translations.literal: I have always loved medical arts, yet did not let my younger brother be preserved whole; again reflecting that my skill was not refined, there was wrongful error—thinking on this one point, especially cruel pain again.
translations.idiomatic: I have always loved the medical arts, yet did not let my younger brother be preserved whole; reflecting again that my skill was not refined and led to wrongful error—on this one point especially, the pain is cruel again.

sentences.zh: 痛酷奈何！

translations.literal: Cruel pain—what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: Cruel pain—what can be done!

sentences.zh: 吾罪奈何！

translations.literal: My guilt—what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: My guilt—what can be done!

sentences.zh: 弟為志，奉親孝，事兄順，雖僮僕無所叱咄，可謂君子不失色于人，不失口於人。

translations.literal: My brother in aspiration served parents with filial piety, served his elder brother with obedience; even toward servants and boys he never shouted or scolded—one may say a gentleman who does not lose color before others, does not lose words before others.
translations.idiomatic: In aspiration my brother served his parents with filial piety and his elder brother with obedience; even toward servants he never shouted or scolded—he may be called a gentleman who never lost his composure or his words before others.

sentences.zh: 沖和淹通，內有皁白，舉動尺寸，吾每咨之。

translations.literal: Mild and penetrating, within he had black and white; in every movement and measure I always consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and penetrating, inwardly discerning right from wrong; in every movement and measure I always consulted him.

sentences.zh: 常云：「兄文骨氣，可推英麗以自許。

translations.literal: He often said: 'Elder brother's writing has bone and spirit; you can extend splendid beauty to claim for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: He often said: 'Elder brother's writing has bone and spirit; you can extend its splendid beauty to claim for yourself.

sentences.zh: 又兄為人矯介欲過，宜每中和。

translations.literal: Also, elder brother as a man is overly stiff and keen—each time you should balance and harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: Also, as a man you are overly stiff and exacting—you should each time balance and harmonize yourself.

sentences.zh: 」道此猶在耳，萬世不復一見，奈何！

translations.literal: ' These words are still in my ears; ten thousand ages will not see him again—what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: ' Those words are still in my ears; for ten thousand ages I shall not see him again—what can be done!

sentences.zh: 唯十紙手跡，封拆儼然，至於思戀不可懷。

translations.literal: Only ten sheets in his hand—sealed and opened, still intact; as for longing, it cannot be held in the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Only ten sheets in his own hand, sealed and opened, still intact; as for longing, it cannot be contained in the breast.

sentences.zh: 及聞吾病，肝心寸絕，謂當以幅巾薄葬之事累汝，奈何反相殯送！

translations.literal: When he heard I was ill, his liver and heart were cut inch by inch; he said the matter of simple headcloth burial should be entrusted to you—who thought you would instead send me to the grave!
translations.idiomatic: When he heard I was ill, his heart was torn inch by inch; he said the matter of a simple headcloth burial should be entrusted to you—who thought you would instead be the one to send me to the grave!

sentences.zh: 弟由來意謂：「婦人雖無子，不宜踐二庭。

translations.literal: My brother from of old meant: 'Though a woman has no son, she should not tread two courtyards.
translations.idiomatic: My brother long held that: 'Though a woman has no son, she should not enter a second household.

sentences.zh: 此風若行，便可家有孝婦」。

translations.literal: If this custom spreads, households can have filial wives.'
translations.idiomatic: If this custom spreads, every household can have a filial widow.'

sentences.zh: 仲長《昌言》，亦其大要。

translations.literal: Zhongchang's Discourses also states its main point.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchang Cui's Discourses also states its main point.

sentences.zh: 劉新婦以刑傷自誓，必留供養；

translations.literal: Lady Liu the new bride, by penal injury, swore herself—she must remain to provide offerings;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu the new bride, by self-inflicted wound, swore herself—she must remain to provide offerings;

sentences.zh: 殷太妃感柏舟之節，不奪其志。

translations.literal: Grand Consort Yin, moved by the integrity of Bo Zhou, did not wrest away her resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Consort Yin, moved by the integrity of the Bo Zhou ode, did not wrest away her resolve.

sentences.zh: 僕射篤順，范夫人知禮，求得左率第五兒，廬位有主。

translations.literal: The Director-in-chief was dutiful and obedient; Lady Fan understood ritual—they obtained the fifth son of the Left Leader; the Lu lineage seat has a master.
translations.idiomatic: The Director-in-chief was dutiful and obedient; Lady Fan understood ritual—they obtained the fifth son of the Left Leader; the Lu lineage seat now has its heir.

sentences.zh: 此亦何益冥然之痛，為是存者意耳。

translations.literal: This too what benefit to dark pain—it is only for the sake of the living's intent.
translations.idiomatic: What benefit is any of this to the dead in darkness—it is only for the sake of the living's feelings.

sentences.zh: 吾窮疾之人，平生意志，弟實知之。

translations.literal: I, a man exhausted by illness, my lifelong intent—my younger brother truly knew it.
translations.idiomatic: I, a man worn out by illness, my lifelong intent—my brother truly knew it.

sentences.zh: 端坐向窗，有何慰適，正賴弟耳。

translations.literal: Sitting upright facing the window—what comfort is there? I truly relied on my younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Sitting upright facing the window—what comfort is there? I truly relied on my brother.

sentences.zh: 過中未來，已自愒望，今云何得立，自省惛毒，無復人理。

translations.literal: Past midday you had not come—I was already desolate in hope; now how can you stand? Reflecting on myself, confused poison—no more human reason.
translations.idiomatic: Past midday you had not come—I was already desolate in hope; now how can you stand firm? Looking inward, I am confused and poisoned—no human reason remains.

sentences.zh: 比煩冤困憊，不能作刻石文，若靈響有識，不得吾文，豈不為恨。

translations.literal: Lately vexing grief and weary exhaustion—I cannot compose an inscribed stone text; if the spirit's echo has awareness and does not receive my writing, would that not be regret?
translations.idiomatic: Lately vexing grief and weary exhaustion keep me from composing an inscribed stone text; if the spirit's echo has awareness and does not receive my writing, would that not be regret?

sentences.zh: 儻意慮不遂，謝能思之如狂，不知所告訴，明書此數紙，無復詞理，略道阡陌，萬不寫一。

translations.literal: If perchance intent and thought do not succeed, I can only think of it like madness, not knowing whom to tell; clearly writing these several sheets, no more words or reason—roughly tracing the paths between fields, ten thousand parts, not one written.
translations.idiomatic: If perchance intent and thought do not succeed, I can only brood on it like madness, not knowing whom to tell; I clearly write these several sheets, no more words or logic—roughly tracing the paths between fields, ten thousand parts, not one written down.

sentences.zh: 阿謙！

translations.literal: A Qian!
translations.idiomatic: A Qian!

sentences.zh: 何圖至此！

translations.literal: Who thought it would come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Who thought it would come to this!

sentences.zh: 誰復視我，誰復憂我！

translations.literal: Who again will look on me? Who again will grieve for me!
translations.idiomatic: Who again will look on me? Who again will grieve for me!

sentences.zh: 他日寶惜三光，割嗜好以祈年，今也唯速化耳。

translations.literal: In other days I treasured the three lights, cut off indulgences to pray for years—now it is only swift transformation.
translations.idiomatic: In other days I treasured sun, moon, and stars, cut off indulgences to pray for long life—now it is only swift transformation.

sentences.zh: 吾豈復支，冥冥中竟復云何。

translations.literal: How can I again support myself? In the dark within, again what shall be?
translations.idiomatic: How can I again support myself? In the darkness beyond, what shall there be?

sentences.zh: 弟懷隨、和之寶，未及光諸文章，欲收作一集，不知忽忽當辦此不？

translations.literal: My brother harbored Sui and He's treasures, not yet brought to light in writings; he wished to gather them into one collection—do you not know whether, in haste, this can be done?
translations.idiomatic: My brother harbored treasures like Sui and He jade, not yet brought to light in his writings; he wished to gather them into one collection—do you not know whether, in haste, this can still be done?

sentences.zh: 今已成服，吾臨靈取常共飲杯，酌自釀酒，寧有仿像不？

translations.literal: Now the mourning garments are already donned; I approach the spirit and take the cup we always drank from together, pour self-brewed wine—is there any likeness?
translations.idiomatic: Now the mourning garments are already donned; I approach the spirit and take the cup we always drank from together, pour self-brewed wine—is there any likeness at all?

sentences.zh: 冤痛！

translations.literal: Wronged pain!
translations.idiomatic: Wronged pain!

sentences.zh: 冤痛！

translations.literal: Wronged pain!
translations.idiomatic: Wronged pain!

sentences.zh: 元嘉三十年，卒，時年三十九。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Yuanjia he died, aged thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Yuanjia he died, at the age of thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 僧謙卒後四旬而微終。

translations.literal: Forty days after Sengqian's death, Wei ended.
translations.idiomatic: Forty days after Sengqian's death, Wei passed away.

sentences.zh: 遺令薄葬，不設轜旐鼓挽之屬，施五尺床，為靈二宿便毀。

translations.literal: His final instructions were for a simple burial, without setting out funeral carriages, banners, drums, or pallbearers; provide a five-foot bed—for the spirit two nights then destroy.
translations.idiomatic: His final instructions were for a simple burial, without funeral carriages, banners, drums, or pallbearers; provide a five-foot bed—for the spirit two nights, then destroy it.

sentences.zh: 以嘗所彈琴置床上，何長史來，以琴與之。

translations.literal: Place the qin he once played on the bed; when Chief Clerk He comes, give him the qin.
translations.idiomatic: Place the qin he once played on the bed; when Chief Clerk He Yan comes, give him the qin.

sentences.zh: 何長史者，偃也。

translations.literal: Director He is Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Director He is He Yan.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons.

sentences.zh: 家人遵之。

translations.literal: The family followed his instructions.
translations.idiomatic: The family followed his instructions.

sentences.zh: 所著文集傳於世。

translations.literal: The collected writings he authored circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The collected writings he authored circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，詔曰：「微棲志貞深，文行惇洽，生自華宗，身安隱素，足以賁茲丘園，惇是薄俗。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, an edict said: 'Wei's lodged ambition was pure and deep, his writing and conduct sincere and harmonious; born of a splendid clan, his person secure in hidden simplicity—enough to adorn these hills and gardens, and make thick this shallow custom.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, an edict said: 'Wang Wei's lodged ambition was pure and deep, his writing and conduct sincere and harmonious; born of a splendid clan, his person secure in hidden simplicity—enough to adorn these hills and gardens and make thick this shallow custom.

sentences.zh: 不幸蚤世，朕甚悼之。

translations.literal: Unfortunate early death—We greatly mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: Unfortunate early death—We greatly mourn him.

sentences.zh: 可追贈秘書監。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Secretariat.'
translations.idiomatic: He may be posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Secretariat.'

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：燕太子吐一言，田先生吞舌而死；

translations.literal: The historian says: The Yan Crown Prince spat one word, and Master Tian swallowed his tongue and died;
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: The Crown Prince of Yan spat one word, and Master Tian swallowed his tongue and died;

sentences.zh: 安邑令戒屠者，閔仲叔去而之沛。

translations.literal: the magistrate of Anyi warned the butcher, and Min Zhongshu left and went to Pei.
translations.idiomatic: the magistrate of Anyi warned the butcher, and Min Zhongshu left and went to Pei.

sentences.zh: 良由內懷耿介，峻節不可輕干。

translations.literal: Truly because within they harbored upright integrity, stern integrity that could not lightly be affronted.
translations.idiomatic: Truly because within they harbored upright integrity—stern integrity that could not lightly be affronted.

sentences.zh: 袁淑笑謔之間，而王微弔詞連牘，斯蓋好名之士，欲以身為珪璋，皦皦然使塵玷之累，不能加也。

translations.literal: Between Yuan Shu's laughter and jest, yet Wang Wei's condolence letters ran sheet on sheet—this is probably a man who loves his name, wishing to make his person jade and regalia, bright and clear so that the burden of dust-stain cannot be added.
translations.idiomatic: Between Yuan Shu's laughter and jest, yet Wang Wei's condolence letters ran sheet on sheet—this is probably a man who loves his name, wishing to make his person jade and regalia, bright and clear so that the burden of dust-stain cannot be added.
